page.layout: One column of text: a title at the top, then six numbered paragraphs, with Hebrew and Greek inside them. Below is the closing word FINIS, then a tailpiece ornament (not transcribed). No running head, page number or catchword.

main_text.head: IMPERTINENTIA
main_text.p: 1. Lingua una, quæ ante confusionem Babyl. obtinuerat, fuit Ebræa.
2. Rectè vertunt LXX. illud Gen. 14. 13. Et nun-tiavit לאברם העברי [?] Ἀβεᾶμ τῷ περάτῃ [?]
3. Indignè tractant scripturam Vet. Test. qui textum Hebræum his vocalibus vestitum non nisi Commentarij Masorethici loco ha-bendum contendunt.
4. Versio LXX. viralis, quæcunque in ejus histo-ria crepentur miracula, non est divinæ au-thoritatis.
5. קרי וכתיב item, תיקון סופרים [?] ac עשור סופרים [?] non arguunt textum Ebræum esse corruptum.
6. Nota Masorethica ad Gen. 4. 8. quæ hæc est; פסוק במצעו פסקי פסוקים כח [?] non præjudicat in-tegritati Scripturæ S.

page.notes: The tailpiece ornament (a flower vase with a mask and a bee) is an engraving and is not transcribed. The Hebrew and Greek are copied from a small, uneven print; the Hebrew in items 2, 5 and 6 and the Greek in item 2 are uncertain, and the Hebrew in item 2 shows a box-like glyph where a letter should be. The Hebrew in item 5 and item 6 is marked [?] because the letter order in the print is hard to confirm. Item 2 Greek is read as Ἀβεᾶμ τῷ περάτῃ, marked [?]. Dark marks on the right edge are scan artefacts and are left out.
